feed.title: HeatWatch
feed.subtitle: Where heat is breaking records, who it is reaching, what the rules are about to require, and what can be done about it.

entry.title: Western Australia's Kimberley is under an extreme heatwave warning from 28 November to 1 December
entry.summary: The Bureau of Meteorology upgraded the Kimberley to extreme on 28 November, with severe warnings for the Pilbara, Gascoyne and North Interior. Fitzroy Crossing reached 44.8 °C on 24 November. — Sources: Bureau of Meteorology, Heatwave Warning for Western Australia IDW21013, issued 13:15 WST 28 November 2026 · Bureau of Meteorology, daily weather observations, Western Australia, 21 to 27 November 2026

entry.title: Australia's weekly El Niño ocean index rose to +2.67 °C after two weekly falls
entry.summary: The relative Niño3.4 index was +2.67 °C for 16 to 22 November, up from +2.64 °C. The Bureau of Meteorology now expects the El Niño peak in December or January. — Sources: Bureau of Meteorology, weekly relative Niño3.4 and Indian Ocean Dipole data files, read 28 November 2026 · Bureau of Meteorology, climate driver update, 24 November 2026

entry.title: Birdsville, Queensland, reached 46.8 °C and Jervois, Northern Territory, 45.1 °C on 22 November
entry.summary: These were the highest readings in Australia for the week. — Sources: Bureau of Meteorology, daily weather observations and station climate statistics, 21 to 27 November 2026

entry.title: Brazil's electricity demand set records on three consecutive days, peaking at 108.17 gigawatts on 25 November
entry.summary: Preliminary grid-operator data show 106.61 GW on 23 November, 108.03 GW on 24 November and 108.17 GW on 25 November, the highest of 2026. The rise is attributed to heat. — Sources: Agência iNFRA, citing preliminary data from Brazil's national grid operator ONS, 26 to 27 November 2026

entry.title: Sydney's severe heatwave peaked at 36.5 °C in Penrith on 22 November and set no records
entry.summary: Richmond reached 36.4 °C, Bankstown 35.2 °C and Parramatta 35.0 °C, while Observatory Hill stayed at 28.1 °C. The warmest night was 23 November, and the warning has ended. — Sources: Bureau of Meteorology, daily weather observations for Sydney stations, 21 to 23 November 2026

entry.title: Weipa, Queensland, keeps its all-time high of 40.4 °C as the Cape York heatwave warning ends
entry.summary: The Bureau of Meteorology cancelled the Peninsula heatwave warning on 27 November. Weipa's maxima from 21 to 27 November ranged from 36.6 to 38.5 °C, and the 40.4 °C record of 19 November stands. — Sources: Bureau of Meteorology, Weipa Aero daily weather observations, November 2026 · Bureau of Meteorology, Queensland heatwave warning cancellation, 13:31 EST 27 November 2026

entry.title: San Juan, Puerto Rico, United States, broke daily heat records on 25 and 26 November
entry.summary: The airport reached 92 °F (33 °C) on 25 November, beating 90 °F from 1981, and 91 °F (33 °C) on 26 November, beating 89 °F from 2024. These follow five record days from 10 to 14 November. — Sources: NOAA Applied Climate Information System, San Juan airport station, 24 to 26 November 2026

entry.title: Peru's weather service issued red-level warnings for high temperatures on the coast and highlands through 2 December
entry.summary: Senamhi warnings 488 and 489, issued 27 November, cover higher daytime and night-time temperatures from 29 November to 2 December, after red warnings for 19 to 28 November. — Sources: Senamhi, avisos meteorológicos 476, 480, 484, 485, 488 and 489, November 2026

entry.title: England has hosepipe bans at 10 water companies, with reservoirs at 60.2 percent
entry.summary: November rainfall is 61 percent of average. Severe drought continues in parts of Devon, Cornwall and Wessex and in parts of Kent, South London and the South Downs, with three drought orders pending. — Sources: Environment Agency, Dry weather and drought in England, 20 to 26 November 2026, published 27 November 2026

entry.title: Brazil's satellites counted 10,989 fire foci from 21 to 27 November, up 76 percent on the week before
entry.summary: The Amazon had 6,587 foci, the Cerrado 2,390 and the Caatinga 1,898. Pará and Maranhão led, and the daily count peaked at 2,571 on 24 November. — Sources: INPE daily fire foci, reference satellite, 21 to 27 November 2026

entry.title: A lightning-started fire burned about 15,320 hectares on Flinders Island, Tasmania, Australia
entry.summary: The fire covered more than a tenth of the island and damaged or destroyed at least eight structures. An emergency warning applied from 25 November, and one firefighter was taken to hospital. — Sources: ABC News, 27 November 2026

entry.title: Indonesia's fire hotspots have moved east to Papua, with 399 counted on 28 November
entry.summary: Daily counts ranged from 307 to about 818 during the week. Papua Selatan led on 28 November with 235, as burning shifted from Kalimantan to Papua, Sulawesi and Maluku. — Sources: SiPongi hotspot counts as reported by Databoks, 21 to 28 November 2026 · National Environment Agency Singapore, 24-hour PSI, 28 November 2026

entry.title: England's health agency estimates 5,258 heat-associated deaths in summer 2026, the highest since its records began
entry.summary: The UK Health Security Agency counts 5,258 deaths from May to September across seven heat episodes, against a previous high of 2,985 in 2022. The 21 to 28 June heatwave accounts for 2,401. — Sources: UK Health Security Agency, Interim heat mortality monitoring report, England: summer 2026, updated 24 November 2026

entry.title: Queensland, the Northern Territory and Western Australia publish no count of heat illness through this season's heatwaves
entry.summary: Australia's northern states and territory have had severe and extreme heatwave warnings since early October with no public series of heat-related hospital or ambulance presentations. — Sources: Bureau of Meteorology heatwave warnings for Queensland, the Northern Territory and Western Australia, October to November 2026 · ABC News, Cape York heat and housing, 14 November 2026
